mission.brief: Your rover needs six continuous hours of direct sunlight after touchdown to collect a sample. Choose a landing site and a touchdown time.
mission.rule: Pass when the entire apparent solar disc stays above the local terrain skyline (seen from the panel height) and clear of Earth for the whole sampling block that starts at touchdown.
mission.hint: Follow the sampling block to its end. Does the Sun clear the ridge the whole time?

conventions.frame: Moon mean-Earth/polar-axis (MEAN_ME / MOON_ME), east longitude positive
conventions.elevation_datum: heights above a 1737.4 km sphere (LOLA and Horizons)
conventions.azimuth: true compass bearing, 0° toward the lunar north pole, increasing clockwise (east = 90°)
conventions.elevation: degrees above the local horizontal plane of the sphere; no refraction (airless)
conventions.sun_full: whole solar disc above the skyline and not overlapped by Earth
conventions.earth_up: centre of Earth's disc above the skyline (a geometric reading; no communications claim)
conventions.display_precision: show times to the minute with the listed uncertainty; angles to 0.1°

sites.name: Apollo 11
sites.terrain_source: LOLA LDEM 118 m (256 px/deg) patch, then LDEM_4 (7.6 km)

intervals.format: sun_full and earth_up: [start_unix, end_unix, start_uncertainty_s, end_uncertainty_s]; sun_any: [start_unix, end_unix]. Ends are the last second inside the interval.
